key_facts: The RECOVER PII Act, to be introduced by Sen. Mark Warner and Del. Eleanor Holmes Norton, would extend identity-protection coverage for 2015 OPM breach victims for life.
Coverage for 22.1 million people affected by the 2015 OPM breaches is currently scheduled to end Sept. 30, 2026.
The 2015 breaches compromised personnel records for roughly 4.2 million people and background-investigation records for 21.5 million people, with about 3.6 million affected by both.
A 2017 appropriations law required OPM to provide at least 10 years of complimentary identity protection and $5 million in identity-theft insurance; the new bill would remove the 10-year limit.
The bill would also allow agencies to reimburse federal employees and contractors for privacy tools that remove or limit personal information online.
